images.title: Two ways to arrange squares
images.purpose: Match 5 × 2 + 3 to one square arrangement and 2 × (5 + 3) to another.
images.composition: Two arrangements side by side with equal space, each with its expression below.
exact_structure: Left: a block of 5 rows by 2 columns of teal #0072B2 squares (10 squares), and below it one separate row of 3 reddish purple #CC79A7 squares, 13 squares in all.
Right: 2 rows, each row made of 5 amber #E69F00 squares followed by 3 teal squares, 16 squares in all.
Squares are equal size with thin dark outlines.
Under the left figure: 5 × 2 + 3 = 13. Under the right figure: 2 × (5 + 3) = 16.
rejection: right figure not showing 2 rows of 8 squares
any square count differing from the stated totals
images.takeaway: The expression follows the way the squares are grouped.
images.description: Left, 10 squares and 3 extra make 13; right, two rows of 5 and 3 make 16.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text on matching expressions to pictures.
images.teaching_notes: Count each group first, then match it to the expression.

image_decisions.why: A picture of grouping is the best way to see why brackets matter.
